hangul.title: The Hangul alphabet
hangul.lead: Hangul has 19 consonants and 21 vowels. Each syllable combines an initial consonant, a vowel and sometimes a final consonant. Click a letter to see how to write it and hear it.
groupNote.plain: Pronounced without a strong puff of air. At the start of a word ㄱ ㄷ ㅂ ㅈ sound close to k, t, p, ch; between vowels they sound like g, d, b, j.
groupNote.aspirated: Pronounced with a strong puff of air – hold a sheet of paper in front of your mouth and it should move.
groupNote.tense: Pronounced with a tense throat and no puff of air, short and sharp – like the k in “sky” or the t in “stop”.
groupNote.basic: The 10 basic vowels are made by adding short strokes to a long line; doubling the short stroke adds a y sound (ㅏ a → ㅑ ya).
groupNote.compound: Vowels formed by combining two basic vowels. In modern speech ㅐ and ㅔ – and ㅙ, ㅚ, ㅞ – sound almost the same.
place.velar: Velar (back of the tongue against the soft palate)
place.alveolar: Alveolar (tip of the tongue against the upper gum ridge)

batchim.title: Final consonants (batchim)
batchim.lead: A consonant at the end of a syllable is called batchim (받침). There are 27 ways to write it, but only 7 sounds.
batchim.linkingLead: When the next syllable starts with ㅇ (no consonant), the final consonant moves over: 음악 is read [으막].
